title: Kochi IT Workers Launch Road Safety Campaign After Colleague Killed by Bus
excerpt: Progressive Techies passed 4,000 signatures in a day after EY consultant Akshara A., 28, was fatally struck at IMG Junction, Kakkanad, and is targeting 20,000 to press authorities to clear the Infopark road.
body:
• Kochi's IT fraternity has launched a road-safety campaign after Akshara A., 28, a senior consultant with EY, was fatally struck by an allegedly speeding bus at IMG Junction, Kakkanad, while walking home from a gym session.
  • Progressive Techies' digital signature campaign passed 4,000 signatures within a day and targets 20,000 before it is sent to the District Collector, the Chief Minister and the Public Works Minister.
  • The main demand is to clear encroachments on the stretch from IMG Junction to Infopark Road and make it safe for pedestrians and motorists.
  • For readers who walk or drive near Infopark: the campaign is a petition for safer infrastructure, not a fundraiser — no verified fundraiser for the family was named in the coverage read.

A death that mobilised a campus

IT professionals based at Infopark in Kochi have launched a multi-pronged road-safety campaign after a colleague was killed by a bus near the campus. Akshara A., 28, a senior consultant with EY, was fatally knocked down by an allegedly speeding bus while walking home after a gym session at IMG Junction, Kakkanad, on Wednesday, according to The Hindu's reporting summarised in syndicated coverage and Mirror Now. Employees from various firms gathered at Infopark on Thursday evening for a candlelit vigil in her memory.

What the campaign is asking for

The campaign is led by Progressive Techies, a collective of IT professionals. Its digital signature campaign garnered over 4,000 signatures within a day. "We are targeting at least 20,000 signatures for our campaign, and once we achieve this, we will forward our complaint to the authorities, including the District Collector, Chief Minister and Public Works Minister," Anish Panthalani, co-founder of Progressive Techies, said.

"The major demand of our campaign is to evict encroachments along the stretch of road from IMG Junction to Infopark Road and make it safe for motorists and pedestrians."

— Progressive Techies, via The Hindu reporting

Panthalani said the risks extend beyond the accident site, pointing to similar concerns on other roads used by tech workers, including Edachira and Pallikkara, and to stray dogs as a further hazard. The group is also exploring a public interest litigation to press for permanent infrastructure improvements.

A second group joins in

The All India Professionals' Congress (AIPC) Infopark chapter has also launched a campaign following Akshara's death. It has scheduled a 'Listening Circle' on campus for employees to voice traffic concerns. Eldho Chirackalchalil, the district president of AIPC, said the organisation has formally raised the safety issues with the Home Minister and the Transport Minister, and is calling for strict legal action against the driver involved in the fatal collision.

What happens next

The test for the campaign is whether signatures convert into cleared footpaths, enforcement against speeding buses, and safer pedestrian space on the IMG Junction–Infopark stretch. For the thousands who walk that route daily, that — not the petition count — is the outcome that matters.
